incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT — elevated 5xx rate on hosted/redwood-prod (gpu-pool-3). Recent container restarts observed; root cause appears to be GPU OOM during prefill for very long prompts. Paging oncall.
sophie: taking this — oncall-eng. Anyone else affected?
ali: seeing a spike of OOMs in the logs from the runtime, repeating `cuCtxSynchronize` failures and `CUDA out of memory` in prefill path. Affected model: redwood-13b-v1 with long context loads.
patrick: exact symptoms: the prefill step blows memory when users submit very long concatenated contexts (12k+ tokens). Containers enter CrashLoopBackOff and kube restarts them, causing bursts of 502/500s.
sophie: confirm, attaching snippet from `runtime.log`:
```
2026-11-09T14:12:07Z ERROR runtime.prefill: Prefill failed: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB (GPU0)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/redwood/runtime/prefill.py", line 312, in run_prefill
    kv_cache.allocate(...)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```
mike: any automated limiter in front of prefill? I remember we had a token cap in the gateway but customers can bypass with streaming chunked inputs.
jess: gateway has a soft `max_context_tokens=65536` in config, but the runtime does not enforce an absolute prefill cap. Streaming clients can submit multiple messages that end up concatenated in prefill.
sophie: mitigation options:
- emergency hotpatch to runtime to reject prefill requests > 8192 tokens with a clear 4xx and guidance to use chunked streaming / shorter prompts
- temporarily route heavy-context requests to a low-priority pool (cpu-fallback or smaller model)
- enable aggressive KV eviction / drop prefill (risky for correctness)
- scale up GPU capacity (slow)

ali: I can roll a hotpatch to add a prefill token check in the request path. Will deploy as a config flag first: `PREFILL_TOKEN_HARD_LIMIT=8192` and return `400` with `error: prefill_token_limit_exceeded`.
sophie: please do that ASAP. Also update status page and notify CS about impacted customers.
deploy-bot: build 9f1c2a -> staging passed, promoting to canary on prod-gpu-3 cluster.
ali: applying patch now on canary subset:
```
kubectl -n redwood patch deployment runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"PREFILL_TOKEN_HARD_LIMIT","value":"8192"}]}]}}}}'
```
patrick: canary looks good for 6 minutes, no OOMs on those pods.
sophie: roll to all gpu-pool-3 nodes. Keep `canary=10%` for the first 5m.
deploy-bot: rollout started -> rollout/patch-runtime-9f1c2a -> 30 pods updating.

(10 minutes later)
ali: hotpatch rolled to 100% of gpu-pool-3. Observed: OOMs dropped to baseline. Container restarts down from ~2/min to 0.
mike: good. Next step: block/route heavy requests. Can we add an immediate routing rule to send requests exceeding 8000 tokens to `redwood-7b-fallback` model?
jess: yes, I can add a routing rule in the control plane. Will create policy `route_large_prefill_to_small`.

jess: policy applied. Example rule:
```
if request.prefill_tokens > 8000:
  route -> model: redwood-7b-fallback, tag: low-priority
  add header: x-prefill-routed: true
```

cs-bot: CS alert: customers reporting intermittent 500s. Known impacted: acme-inc (large-doc-import), beta-corp (chat transcripts). CS will prepare customer comms and recommended mitigations for them.
sophie: please add an incident note for acme-inc and mention recommended workaround — split large document into chunks <8k tokens or use the batch upload job.
cs-bot: done — ticket INC-4521 created and customers notified.

ali: postmortem items already noted in the incident board:
- runtime should enforce prefill hard limits by default
- add telemetry: per-request prefill token count metric
- evaluate streaming prefill logic to avoid implicit concatenation
- add integration test: long-context load test that simulates 12k tokens

patrick: immediate follow-ups:
- create a perf/regression test and run on release pipeline (owner: ali)
- update runbook with new prefill hard limit and routing (owner: jess) — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom
- schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT (owner: sophie)

sophie: handing to mike for overnight oncall monitoring. I'll be offline in 30m.
mike: taking over. I'll keep an eye on gpu-pool-3, OOM metrics, and customer tickets. If anything spikes, page me.

(automated summary)
incident-bot: SUMMARY: GPU OOMs during prefill caused container restarts on gpu-pool-3. Hotpatch applied (PREFILL_TOKEN_HARD_LIMIT=8192) and routing rule to fallback model created. Impact: short-lived 5xx spikes affecting a small set of customers with very large contexts. Follow-ups and postmortem scheduled.

sophie: :white_check_mark: closing out live mitigation. Save logs and evidence to the incident folder: `s3://redwood-incidents/1901012345/` and attach to INC-4521.
patrick: logs archived and evidence attached.

mike: ack, will monitor and escalate if we see regressions. Thanks team. :heart:
